---
title: "Validate a collection of forms"
output: html_document
---

Use this workflow for a collection needing individual reports, aggregates, code-list evidence and registry evidence.

## Prepare inputs and references

Install the packages using the home page instructions. Run all commands below in the same R session.

Keep inputs under `<year>/<country>/<gear>/v<version>/`, using `LL` or `PS` for gear:

```text
ros-input-data/
  2024/
    EU-SPAIN/
      PS/
        v3.3.0/
          submitted-form.xlsx
```

The year and country come from directory names. Keep original filenames. Excel lock files are excluded.

Obtain an approved reference snapshot for each selected model version before planning.

## 1. Plan the work

Edit the paths below. The output must be outside the input directory.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
library(ros.form.validation)

input <- "ros-input-data"
references <- c(
  "3.3.0" = "references/3.3.0",
  "4.0.0" = "references/4.0.0",
  "4.1.0" = "references/4.1.0"
)
stamp <- format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%dT%H%M%SZ", tz = "UTC")
batch <- file.path("output", paste0("ros-validation-", stamp))
plan <- plan_ros_validation(
  input = input,
  references = references,
  versions = names(references),
  output = batch
)
plan$jobs
batch
```

Planning saves the selected inputs, rules and reference values. It does not validate the forms yet.

Text-cell boundaries are trimmed by readxl. Add `trim_ws = FALSE` to preserve surrounding whitespace.

The reader choice is saved in the plan. Internal whitespace and native cell types are preserved.

META content errors are warnings by default. Add `meta_as_warnings = FALSE` to keep original rule severities.

This choice is saved in the plan and shown in each form report. Create a new plan to change it.

Three versions with both gears produce six jobs. Jobs with no forms remain visible in the plan.

Keep the printed batch path: you will use it to resume the run after closing R.

To limit a run, add `country = "EU-SPAIN"`, `year = "2024"` or `gear = "ps"` to the planning call.

## 2. Validate every planned form

```{r, eval=FALSE}
validation <- validate_ros_plan(plan)
validation$jobs
```

This saves validation results without generating reports. It can resume after an interruption.

Do not change the inputs during the run. Changed forms or reference values require a new plan.

## 3. Generate individual reports

```{r, eval=FALSE}
reports <- write_ros_reports(plan)
reports
```

Reports are written under the batch's `reports/` directory, following the input hierarchy.

This stage reads saved results; it does not reopen the submitted forms.

## 4. Build the folder to share

```{r, eval=FALSE}
publication <- build_ros_publication(plan, comment = "Text-cell boundaries trimmed before validation.")
publication
```

The new folder is `output/aggregated_ros-validation-<timestamp>`, alongside the raw batch.

It contains form reports, ancestor aggregates, code-list evidence and registry evidence. Nothing is uploaded yet.

The optional comment is saved in `publication.json` and shown beside the batch after publication.

## 5. Review and share

```{r, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("servr") # Once, for local report previews
servr::httd(dir = publication, browser = TRUE)
```

Start at the root report and follow its cards, tables and breadcrumbs to the individual forms.

Read [Understand results](understand-results.html) before deciding which submissions need follow-up.

See [Resume and share results](resume-and-share.html) for interrupted runs and handing the folder to your web operator.
